problem_motivation.content: Increasing strength without sacrificing tensile ductility remains difficult.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: it remains challenging to increase the strength of these alloys without seriously compromising their tensile ductility

problem_motivation.content: Combining strength above 2 GPa and ductility above 10 percent is a long-standing challenge.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: achieving alloys with an ultrahigh strength (>2 GPa) and a sufficient ductility (>10%) has presented a long-standing challenge

causal_claim.content: Annealing at 900 degrees C rapidly forms coherent delta nanolamellae.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Coherent δ nano-lamellae appeared rapidly during the initial stage of annealing at 900 °C

mechanism_principle.content: Delta and gamma-double-prime precipitates form by diffusional transformation.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: the growth and coarsening of the δ and γ ″ phases, shown in Fig. 2c–f , are both controlled by the sub-micrometer diffusion, which indicates that the formation of both type of precipitates is the result of a diffusional transformation

hypothesis_statement.content: Stepwise coherent nanoprecipitation can defeat the strength-ductility tradeoff.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: we put forward a strategy to “defeat” this trade-off in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys by stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs)

hypothesis_statement.content: Coherent interfaces transmit dislocations and relieve crack-forming stress.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The coherent interfaces of SCCPs facilitate the dislocation transmission and relieve the stress concentrations that can lead to premature crack initiation

evidence_result.content: The alloy reached 2.15 GPa and 15 percent ductility.
evidence_result.evidence_span: our alloy displays an ultrahigh strength of 2.15 GPa with a tensile ductility of 15% at ambient temperature

contradiction.content: Unlike conventional W alloys, coherent delta interfaces suppress microcrack initiation.
contradiction.evidence_span: Unlike traditional W-based heavy alloys where intermetallic compounds invariably act as the origin of microcracks from major dislocation pile-ups during deformation, the coherent interface of the δ phase in the W-based HEA effectively alleviates this problem
